introduction_markdown: This paper is arranged in two sections, A and B. Answer ALL questions in Sections A and B. Section A: Answer ALL the questions in the spaces provided (15 questions); the mark allocation for each question is indicated. Section B: Answer ALL FOUR questions in this section; all questions in Section B carry equal marks (15 marks each). You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Duration: two and a half hours.
incertitudes: Q B4 : barème imprimé par bloc ((i) 9 marks, (ii) 6 marks), rappelé dans l'énoncé de (d) et de (ii)(b). Les parties (i)(a)-(d) sont numérotées a à d et (ii)(a)-(b) numérotées e et f. Le graphe est à tracer par l'élève : le corrigé donne le tableau de valeurs, les points clés et les lectures attendues (solutions 0 et 3 ; maximum 2,25 en x = 1,5, lecture graphique attendue environ 2,2 à 2,3). Le sujet imprimé écrit « -1 <= x <= 4 ».

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Given the function $f(x)=3x-x^2$ defined for $-1\le x\le4$.

(a) Construct a table of values of $y=f(x)$ for integral values of $x$ in the range.
(b) Using a scale of $2$ cm to represent $1$ unit on both axes, draw the graph of $y=f(x)$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Axes: $x$ from $-1$ to $4$ and $y$ from $-4$ to $3$, with $2$ cm per unit on both axes.

Plot the six points $(-1,-4)$, $(0,0)$, $(1,2)$, $(2,2)$, $(3,0)$, $(4,-4)$. For more accuracy, add $(0.5,1.25)$, $(1.5,2.25)$ and $(2.5,1.25)$.

Join the points with a smooth curve (no ruler). The curve is an upside-down parabola (an n-shape) that is symmetrical about the line $x=1.5$, with its highest point at $(1.5,2.25)$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
From your graph,

(c) solve the equation $3x-x^2=0$,
questions.corrige_markdown:
The solutions of $3x-x^2=0$ are the $x$-values where the curve cuts the $x$-axis ($y=0$): the curve crosses at $x=0$ and $x=3$.

(Algebra check: $x(3-x)=0$ gives $x=0$ or $x=3$.)

**$x=0$ or $x=3$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (d) state the maximum value of $f(x)$. *[9 marks for (i)]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The maximum value is the $y$-value at the highest point of the curve, which lies on the axis of symmetry $x=\dfrac{0+3}{2}=1.5$.

$f(1.5)=3(1.5)-(1.5)^2=4.5-2.25=2.25$.

**Maximum value of $f(x)=2.25$** (read from the graph at $x=1.5$).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) Given the polynomial $p(x)=(x-2)(2x-1)(x+1)$.

(a) Solve the equation $p(x)=0$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A product is zero when one of its factors is zero:

$x-2=0\Rightarrow x=2$; $\ 2x-1=0\Rightarrow x=\dfrac12$; $\ x+1=0\Rightarrow x=-1$.

**$x=2$, $x=\dfrac12$ or $x=-1$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Find the remainder when $p(x)$ is divided by $(x-1)$. *[6 marks for (ii)]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
By the remainder theorem, the remainder when $p(x)$ is divided by $(x-1)$ is $p(1)$.

$p(1)=(1-2)(2\times1-1)(1+1)=(-1)(1)(2)=-2$.

(Check by expanding: $p(x)=2x^3-3x^2-3x+2$, so $p(1)=2-3-3+2=-2$.)

**Remainder $=-2$.**
